A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Uni-MuMER and contain readable main text, figures, tables, and complete appendices. Existing material can be matched across renumbering and relocation; v3 substantially expands the empirical evaluation.

before.justification: v1 reports original recognition experiments, component ablations, data-scaling experiments, efficiency measurements, and qualitative analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds general multimodal evaluations, leave-one-dataset-out experiments, representation ablations, and error and filtering analyses.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure remains full VLM fine-tuning with Vanilla HMER, Tree-CoT, out-of-fold error detection/correction data, and Symbol Counting, followed by direct LaTeX inference. The larger-model, mixed-data, and alternative-format experiments do not replace the core method.

E1.justification: Section 5.3 adds LLaVA-OneVision training data and evaluates general multimodal understanding and mathematical reasoning on MMMU_val, Math-Vision, and MathVista_testmini. Appendix C.5 also evaluates CJK-containing HME100K samples previously excluded from recognition experiments. CROHME2023, MNE, MathWriting, and printed-expression coverage already existed in v1.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated ICAL and UniMERNet rows; the new CROHME2023 comparison includes TST and TST with external data. MathWriting gains Vanilla and dataset-specific Uni-MuMER comparisons. DenseWAP's CROHME2019 comparison is withdrawn. These extend or adjust an otherwise largely retained comparator suite.

E3.justification: v3 adds leave-one-dataset-out training, a 1:1 HMER/LLaVA mixture, a 7B configuration, CJK inclusion/exclusion controls, hallucination/omission metrics, and evaluation on the original unnormalized Im2LaTeXv2 test set. Existing reported settings also change: the main-text image count becomes 386K instead of 392K, and Appendix B.4 reports 3152 rather than 3125 optimization steps. These revisions do not establish which existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component, complexity, repetition, and cumulative-data analyses, v3 tests dependence on individual training domains, model size, AST serialization, and counting formats. Appendix C.4 quantifies hallucinations and omissions by token type; C.5 tests filtering effects, and D.2 examines normalization sensitivity. These substantially broaden the investigation of design choices and failure conditions.

E5.justification: v1 provides point estimates without specifying run counts. v3's checklist explicitly states that each configuration was run once and that no error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests are reported. This newly discloses the statistical practice; it does not demonstrate a changed run budget.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial results for the new evaluations and analyses, plus CROHME2023 and MathWriting entries. Uni-MuMER with external data changes from 71.93/73.67 to 72.66/74.30 for HME100K ExpRate/ExpRate@CDM, and from 84.32/88.99 to 88.19/93.29 in the principal printed-expression table. Figure 6 also changes. These are revised reported results, not established same-setting gains; v3 itself retains 88.99 for printed ExpRate@CDM in Table 17 while reporting 93.29 in Table 24.

T1.justification: Appendix C.4 introduces limited quantitative definitions: HTR is the percentage of predicted tokens absent from the ground truth, and MTR is the percentage of ground-truth tokens absent from the prediction, with token-type subdivisions. Neither version develops theoretical guarantees or proofs; the existing mathematical exposition and CDM counterexample remain.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same unified fine-tuning contribution, three auxiliary tasks, and headline advantages over SSAN and Gemini2.5-flash. The revised conclusion emphasizes accuracy, scalability, and speed already claimed in v1. Wording such as 'super SOTA' does not substantively change those claims.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 shifts emphasis from domain-specific training necessity toward qualified held-out-domain generalization. New discussions interpret general-data mixing tradeoffs, representation compactness, token-error mechanisms, and CJK filtering. The limitations replace the absence of general VLM evaluation with unexplored task/domain mixture ratios. The unused synthetic-data limitation and CDM caveat are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix B.4 changes the reported training resources from four A800 GPUs and 78 hours to eight A800 GPUs and 20 hours; D.2 adds explicit normalization examples. Reporting remains inconsistent: the new checklist instead states four A800s and 96 hours, and describes a future code release despite the retained abstract's open-source claim. Actual resource availability cannot be resolved from these PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to TST and the Character Detection Matching paper and removes Elman's 'Finding Structure in Time.' Most other reference changes update metadata for the same works. Section 2 and the positioning against specialized architectures remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include localized copyediting, renamed headings, a rewritten conclusion, clearer appendix references, author/header edits, and added acknowledgements and a conference checklist. New analyses extend the existing structure without extensively reorganizing the original narrative.

P2.justification: v3 adds substantial tables for transfer, general benchmarks, representation choices, hallucinations, CJK effects, and CROHME2023. Existing tables gain rows or separate evaluation blocks, particularly the normalized/unnormalized printed comparison. Table 1 gains model-category headings, and Figure 6 has revised plotting and axis limits. The original framework and case-study figures are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses v1's explicitly acknowledged lack of general VLM evaluation and adds meaningful controls for domain transfer, representation choices, CJK filtering, and normalization. These experiments substantially strengthen the evidence behind the method and expose its boundaries. Single-run estimates and conflicting compute, release, and printed-score reporting limit confidence and reproducibility, but the expanded validation provides a substantial net improvement.
